data.content:
Gongmen Gate
Gongmen Gate is the gate outside which the events take place involving characters like Fan Li and A Qing.

Xi Shi
Xi Shi is the famous beauty from the Yue kingdom, associated with the Huan Sha Creek, sent into the Wu palace.<SEP>Xi Shi is a beautiful woman gifted to King Fuchai of Wu as part of Yue’s strategy to distract and weaken his governance.<SEP>Xi Shi is a woman cherished by Fan Li and A Qing, who is wounded by A Qing’s bamboo stick but admired for her beauty.<SEP>Xi Shi is a woman living in Guangwa Palace and shares tender moments with Fan Li.

A Qing
A Qing is a young woman who cares deeply for her sheep named Lao Bai and shows simple innocence and joy despite hardships.<SEP>A Qing is a young and naive countryside girl who learns exquisite sword skills from Bai Gonggong and tends sheep with Fan Li.<SEP>A Qing is a skilled fighter who wields a bamboo staff and demonstrates exceptional swordsmanship and combat ability against multiple opponents.<SEP>A Qing is a young woman regarded as a close friend by Fan Li and Xi Shi, notable for her military skill and strong feelings toward Xi Shi.

Guards
Guards are soldiers commanded by Fan Li to protect the palace gates, including 1,000 armored soldiers and 1,000 swordsmen.

Palace
Palace is the location where Fan Li, Xi Shi, and A Qing's confrontation occurs, including the Guan Wa Gong area.

Taihu Lake
Taihu Lake is the place to which Fan Li plans to escape by boat with Xi Shi.

Bamboo Stick
A lightweight bamboo stick used by the young girl as a weapon with agile and skilled moves, capable of stabbing and disabling opponents.<SEP>A weapon wielded by the girl used to blind opponents and strike with high agility and skill.<SEP>The bamboo stick is used by A Qing and Bai Gonggong for playful combat and is the medium through which A Qing learned her swordsmanship.<SEP>Bamboo Stick is used by Bai Gonggong when playing or teaching sword-like techniques to A Qing during shepherding.<SEP>The bamboo stick is a weapon wielded by A Qing during her attack in the palace.

Thousand Armored Soldiers
Thousand Armored Soldiers are a group of soldiers guarding the palace as ordered by Fan Li.

Thousand Swordsmen
Thousand Swordsmen are another group of palace defenders guarding the gates alongside the armored soldiers.

Qingyi Swordsman
Qingyi Swordsman is a sword warrior wearing green clothes who demonstrates exceptional sword skills and participates in multiple duels against opponents.

Wei Shi
Wei Shi are palace guards who respond quickly to the breach and run to the palace gates after A Qing enters.

Jinshan Swordsman
Jinshan Swordsman is a sword warrior wearing brocade clothes wielding a heavy great sword weighing around fifty jin, engaging in fierce sword battles against Qingyi Swordsmen.

Great Sword
The Great Sword is a heavy weapon weighing approximately fifty jin, used by the Jinshan Swordsman in combat.

Long Sword
The Long Sword is a sword type exceeding five feet in length with a thick blade, wielded by a burly combatant in the duel.<SEP>The Long Sword is a sharp blade wielded by the Qingyi Swordsman, capable of cutting heavy weapons and inflicting serious injuries.<SEP>A sharp, long sword wielded by the guards and Wu Country swordsmen, capable of precise and deadly strikes including splitting goats and attacking enemies.

Wangzhe
Wangzhe is the king overseeing the sword contests and rewarding participants.

Sword Contest
The Sword Contest is a martial arts competition involving duels between Qingyi Swordsmen and Jinshan Swordsmen under Wangzhe's supervision.

Official
The official is a figure commanding the sword practitioners to uphold the way of the sword, possessing a stern and authoritative demeanor.<SEP>The Official is a tall, skinny man around forty years old who commands the Wu-Yue swordsmen to the second duel.<SEP>The Official is a court attendant standing beside Wangzhe who announces sword contest conditions and praises swordsmanship.

Qingyi Swordsman Team
The Qingyi Swordsman Team consists of eight green-clothed swordsmen who participate in the contests against the Jinshan Swordsman Team.

Eastern Hall
Eastern Hall is the location within the palace where the sword contests are observed.

Jinshan Swordsman Team
The Jinshan Swordsman Team is a larger group of over fifty brocade-clothed swordsmen competing against the Qingyi Swordsman Team.

Swordsmanship Technique
Swordsmanship Technique refers to the martial skills and combat methods used by the swordsmen during the contest.

Swordsmanship Reward
Swordsmanship Reward refers to rewards such as gold and wine given by Wangzhe to swordsmen who perform excellently.

Four Versus Four Duel
The Four Versus Four Duel is a sword contest match involving four Qingyi Swordsmen fighting against four Jinshan Swordsmen.

Two Versus Two Duel
The Two Versus Two Duel is a sword contest match involving two Qingyi Swordsmen fighting against two Jinshan Swordsmen.

Jinshan Swordsmen
Jinshan Swordsmen are a group of sword fighters wearing brocade robes who support the Yue King and act as palace guards, engaging in combat during the event.

Swordsman
A swordsman is a participant in the sword contests, either in the Qingyi or Jinshan teams, demonstrating various sword fighting moves and strategies during duels.

Yue King Goujian
The Yue King Goujian is the ruler of Yue Kingdom, who endured defeat by Wu, secretly trains troops to avenge losses, and shows admiration for the swordsmanship of Wu’s swordsmen.

Qingyi Swordsmen
Qingyi Swordsmen are a group of eight sword warriors wearing blue clothes sent by King Fucha of Wu as envoys to present gifts and participate in sword fighting.

Wu King Fucha
Wu King Fucha is the ruler of Wu Kingdom who defeated Yue in the past and sends eight Qingyi swordsmen as envoys bearing gifts.

Swordsmanship
Swordsmanship refers to the skill and techniques of sword fighting displayed by the Qingyi swordsmen and admired by others.<SEP>Swordsmanship refers to A Qing’s skill in combat using a bamboo stick which resembles sword fighting techniques.

Gift Sword
The Gift Sword is a newly forged, three-foot long, very thin sword with a shifting treasure glow, presented as a gift from Wu Kingdom to Yue King Goujian.

Gold-Lacquered Sword Box
The gold-lacquered sword box is a lightweight container used to deliver the gift sword from Wu to Yue, surprising those who see it.

Fan Li
Fan Li is a prominent historical and legendary figure associated primarily with the Kingdom of Yue, known for his multifaceted roles as a minister, advisor, strategist, commander, and protector. He served as a close advisor to King Goujian of Yue, offering strategic counsel across military, political, and metallurgical domains, demonstrating his deep knowledge of swordsmanship and resource management.

Fan Li is depicted as a keen observer and negotiator in matters involving swords and diplomacy. He skillfully handles sword tests, appreciating the sharpness and craftsmanship of swords forged according to the famous techniques of Ou Yezi, one of the ancient masters of sword-making. He was involved in overseeing the forging of thousands of sharp swords, directing craftsmen under supervisors like Xue Zhu, and personally leading elite sword users, showcasing his leadership in military preparations.

In diplomatic contexts, Fan Li acted with restraint and wisdom, prohibiting his guards from killing envoy swordsmen from Wu Country, maintaining order during tense confrontations. He also engaged in negotiations by offering fair compensation and sought to avoid unnecessary bloodshed, reflecting both his strategic mind and ethical considerations.

Fan Li is portrayed as a man of unique insight and eccentric behavior, respected locally for his wisdom. His understanding extended to the control and distribution of metal resources, including suspicion over tin mine control, and the timing necessary for forging quality swords. This metallurgical knowledge underpinned his strategic advice to King Goujian in preparing for conflict.

Beyond his public roles, Fan Li is also remembered as a protector and benefactor in personal and emotional contexts. He cared deeply for individuals such as A Qing and Xi Shi, legendary figures linked to the Yue Kingdom’s history and folklore. He ensured the dignified burial of Lao Bai and promised ongoing support to A Qing’s family to relieve their burdens. Moreover, he shared personal time with A Qing, tending sheep together and waiting for key figures like Bai Gonggong, highlighting his compassionate nature alongside his political acumen. When A Qing disappeared, Fan Li commanded searches for her, further emphasizing his protective role.

Fan Li’s observations also extended to broader geopolitical struggles, including commentary on the rise and fate of figures like Wu Zixu and the conflicts involving the state of Wu, indicating his strategic awareness of the regional power dynamics during his time.

In summary, Fan Li emerges as a complex and influential figure—skilled in swordsmanship, metal resource strategy, military command, and diplomacy, while also demonstrating deep personal loyalty and protective kindness. His legacy intertwines practical statecraft, military leadership, cultural wisdom, and human compassion within the historical and legendary tapestry of the Yue Kingdom.

Xianshi
Xianshi is a master who originally forged three treasured swords for the King of Chu.

Sword Techniques
Sword Techniques refer to the mixed defensive and offensive fighting styles used by the four Qingyi swordsmen in battle.

King Of Chu
The King of Chu is the ruler who treasured three swords forged by Xianshi and gifted one to Feng Shixiong.

Longyuan
Longyuan is one of the three swords forged by Xianshi for the King of Chu.

Taia
Taia is one of the three swords forged by Xianshi for the King of Chu.

Gongbu
Gongbu is one of the three swords forged by Xianshi for the King of Chu.

Feng Shixiong
Feng Shixiong is a master who came into possession of the Gongbu sword through transfer and was a disciple linked with Xianshi.

Goujian
Goujian is a figure discussing the history and significance of the treasured swords and characters involved.<SEP>Goujian is a king who acknowledges the skill and insight of others and shows anger towards enemies.<SEP>Goujian is the King of Yue, discussing swordsmiths and commissioning swords.<SEP>Goujian is a king who led the Yue army in a campaign against Wu.<SEP>Goujian is the leader who initiated the military campaign against Wu three years later.

Xue Zhu
Xue Zhu is a character reporting conversations and events regarding the swords, Feng Shixiong, and Wu general Wu Zixu.<SEP>Xue Zhu is a disciple of Ou Yezi residing in Yue.<SEP>Xue Zhu is tasked by Fan Li to oversee artisan production of many sharp swords.<SEP>Xue Zhu was appointed by Fan Li to oversee skilled craftsmen in forging countless sharp swords.

Wu Zixu
Wu Zixu is a Wu state general who retrieved the Gongbu sword from the tomb of King Ping of Chu and used political influence to gift it to Feng Shixiong.<SEP>Wu Zixu is a talented and reformist advisor in the State of Wu, highly respected for his policies and military insights.<SEP>Wu Zixu is a commander who arranges gifts to summon a person to support Feng Shige in forging swords and has military control over Xishan.

King Ping Of Chu
King Ping of Chu is a ruler whose coffin was desecrated by Wu Zixu, leading to the discovery of the Gongbu sword.

Wu Kingdom
The Wu Kingdom is the state involved in conflict with Chu, where Wu Zixu served as a high-ranking official and manipulated Feng Shixiong.<SEP>Wu Kingdom is a state mentioned as possessing some of Ou Yezi’s swords and being the current residence of Feng Huzi.<SEP>Wu Kingdom is the rival kingdom defeated by Yue warriors trained by Bai Gonggong’s swordsmanship.

Wu General
Wu General refers generally to the military leaders of the Wu Kingdom, including Wu Zixu.

Ganjiang
Ganjiang is a famous swordsmith who previously forged swords but died in the process of forging a treasured sword.

Moye
Moye is the spouse or counterpart of Ganjiang associated with the forging of treasured swords.

Woodun Mountain
Woodun Mountain is the location of the sword forging workshop where Feng Shixiong and Wu Zixu conducted mass sword making.

Sword Forging Workshop
The workshop on Woodun Mountain where over a thousand swordsmiths forged weapons under Feng Shixiong’s guidance.

Wen Zhong
An advisor summoned by King Goujian to discuss the difficult situation after the sword test.<SEP>Wen Zhong is another advisor alongside Fan Li and Goujian, engaged in discussing strategic affairs.<SEP>Wen Zhong is a political strategist who admires Fan Li's distinct views, leaves official duty to follow Fan Li to the State of Wu, and helps plan military and political strategies for the State of Yue.<SEP>Wen Zhong is an adviser who encourages sword casting and values the contributions of swordsmiths.<SEP>Wen Zhong is an adviser who reports about Ou Yezi’s disciples.<SEP>Wen Zhong is a visitor to Fan Li's estate, concerned about Fan Li’s unusual behavior and regarded Fan Li as a good friend.

Warring States Conflict
The struggle for dominance between Wu kingdom and northern states Qi and Jin involving military tactics and weaponry.

Sword Making
The art and method of forging swords, involving ancient techniques and great effort as described in the forging of treasure swords.

Sharp Swords
The large quantity of finely forged swords produced by Feng Shixiong and Wu Zixu to equip Wu soldiers.<SEP>Sharp Swords are the thousands of swords produced under Xue Zhu’s supervision as ordered by Fan Li.

Wu Soldiers
Wu Soldiers are the military forces of the Wu Kingdom, equipped with the sharp swords forged under Feng Shixiong’s supervision.

White Ape
The White Ape is a powerful non-human opponent wielding a bamboo stick, engaging in fast and skillful combat with A Qing.

Wu Kingdom Swordsmen
The Wu Kingdom Swordsmen are warriors from Wu Kingdom who previously fought with A Qing and one was blinded by her in combat.

Yue Kingdom Swordsmen
The Yue Kingdom Swordsmen are elite sword fighters who failed to withstand A Qing’s bamboo staff skill but witnessed her influence on sword techniques.

Kuaiji City
Kuaiji City is an area where Fan Li’s men searched extensively for the missing A Qing.

God Sword Technique
The God Sword Technique is a remarkable and nearly unbeatable sword fighting style inspired by A Qing’s bamboo staff technique and spread among Yue swordsmen.

Five Lakes
The Five Lakes is the battlefield where Goujian’s army fought against Wu.

Yue Army
The Yue Army is led by Goujian and fought at the Five Lakes battle with a force of five thousand soldiers.<SEP>The military force of Yue, numbering 5,000, that advanced with long swords at the Battle of Wuhu.

Bamboo Staff
The Bamboo Staff is a weapon used by A Qing and the White Ape in their combat, characterized by swift and skillful maneuvers and strikes.

Small Girl
The Small Girl refers to A Qing, who disappeared leaving behind an empty house and about a dozen goats.

Goats
A group of about a dozen goats remained in A Qing’s empty house after her disappearance.

Guard
Guards under Fan Li's command who are armed with swords and protect their lord, they surround and confront the Wu Country swordsmen.<SEP>The Guard is ordered by Fan Li to sew Lao Bai’s body and bury it beside A Qing’s house.

Wu Country Swordsman
A swordsman from Wu Country who leads a group of eight swordsmen and demonstrates superior swordsmanship, including slicing a goat in two and engaging in conflict with guards and a young girl.

Young Girl
A slender young girl wearing a light green garment who drives a herd of mountain goats and defends herself skillfully with a bamboo stick against Wu Country swordsmen.

Mountain Goats
A herd of dozen or so mountain goats being herded by the young girl through the street where the Wu Country swordsmen stand.

Gusu
Gusu is the originating place of the Wu Country swordsmen before traveling to Kuaiji.

Kuaiji
Kuaiji is the location where the Wu Country swordsmen arrive and confront Fan Li's guards.

Wu Country Swordsmen Leader
The leading swordsman among the eight Wu Country swordsmen who displays arrogance, sword skill, and leads the group in confrontation with Fan Li’s guards and the young girl.

Wu Country Swordsmen Group
A group of eight swordsmen from Wu Country acting as envoys who challenge opposition despite expecting death.

Fan Chai
A ruler implied to be the overlord or superior of Wu Country, whose anger Fan Li wishes to avoid by not escalating the conflict.

Six Wu Country Swordsmen
A subgroup of the Wu Country swordsmen who are surprised and angry during the conflict and react to the young girl's attacks.

Lao Bai
Lao Bai is a sheep that was killed and its body severed, deeply mourned and cared for by A Qing.

Mother of A Qing
The mother of A Qing advises selling sheep for money but is unaware of Fan Li’s promise to provide rice and cloth.

The House
The house is Fan Li’s large residence where A Qing is invited to stay and where sheep are kept in the garden.

Bai Gonggong
Bai Gonggong is an elderly man living in the mountains who plays with A Qing using bamboo sticks and is implied to have taught her martial arts skills.<SEP>Bai Gonggong is an elderly man who teaches a young countryside girl mysterious swordsmanship and can train warriors of Yue to defeat Wu.

Garden
The garden is part of Fan Li’s estate where a herd of goats eat various flowers under Fan Li’s observation.

Mountain
The mountain is where Bai Gonggong lives and where Fan Li and A Qing go to herd sheep.

Sheep Herd
The herd of sheep (and mountain goats) that A Qing takes care of and brings to Fan Li’s estate.

Cloth
Cloth is material that Fan Li promises to send to A Qing’s family as support.

Rice
Rice is a staple food that Fan Li promises to provide to A Qing’s family to replace income lost by not selling sheep.

Fan Fu
Fan Fu refers to Fan Li as a gentleman; he is mentioned indirectly through staff describing his mysterious behavior.

Chu Kingdom
Chu Kingdom is a state described as the current possessor of the Zhan Lu sword and the original recipient of three swords forged by Ou Yezi.<SEP>The Chu Kingdom is the region where Fan Li was called "Fan Madman" due to his unconventional behavior.

Xiangfei
Xiangfei is a figure from Chu Kingdom folklore known as the Xiangfei and mountain ghost, described in Fan Li’s stories to A Qing.

Northern Direction
Northern direction is the orientation Fan Li looks toward when thinking about the beautiful woman in the Wu King’s palace in Gusu city.

Xishi
Xishi is a beautiful woman whom Fan Li has seen and describes in great detail, contrasting with Xiangfei.

Wu King
Wu King is the ruler residing in Gusu city, possibly accompanied or contemplated by Xishi.

Gusu City
Gusu City is the location of the Wu King’s palace where the beautiful woman Xishi resides.

Green Shadow
Green Shadow is a swift figure who suddenly appears and fiercely engages in combat with White Shadow near Fan Li.

White Shadow
White Shadow is a swift figure who arrives and fights Green Shadow; Bai Gonggong is associated with this figure.

Sheep Herding
Sheep herding is the activity Fan Li and A Qing engage in together in the mountains while waiting for Bai Gonggong.

data.entity_name: Story of Xiangfei and Mountain Ghost
data.content:
Story of Xiangfei and Mountain Ghost
This story is told by Fan Li to A Qing, involving the folklore figures Xiangfei and the mountain ghost.

Staff
Staff members serve under Fan Li and report his unusual behavior to Wen Zhong.

State Of Wu
The State of Wu is a powerful southeastern kingdom with a rising influence, ruled by King Fuchai and advised by Wu Zixu.

State Of Yue
The State of Yue is a neighboring kingdom to Wu, smaller in size but culturally similar, ruled by King Goujian.

Shi Mai
Shi Mai is a general appointed by King Goujian who suffered a major defeat beside the Qiantang River.

King Goujian
The King who tests the sword, expresses determination to defeat Fu Chai, and orders the swordsmen to leave after the demonstration.<SEP>King Goujian is the ruler of the State of Yue, initially defeated by Wu, later employing strategies of Wen Zhong and Fan Li to rebuild strength and seek revenge.

King Fuchai
King Fuchai is the ruler of the State of Wu who ignored Wu Zixu's counsel, eventually making peace and releasing King Goujian before being manipulated.<SEP>The King of Wu who retreated to Yuhang Mountain after the defeat and eventually committed suicide.

Tai Zai Bo Pi
Tai Zai Bo Pi is a treacherous minister in King Fuchai's court, bribed by Yue to influence the Wu king.

Respected Divine Forces
The first of the Nine Military Strategies involves honoring the heavens and spirits to strengthen King Goujian's resolve.

Lavish Gifts To Wu
The second strategy involves sending large quantities of wealth to encourage Wu's decadence and reduce vigilance.

Nine Military Strategies
The Nine Military Strategies are a set of tactics devised by Wen Zhong to defeat Wu, including respect for divine forces, economic sabotage, political manipulation, and military preparation.

Grain Loan And Sabotage
The third strategy is borrowing grain from Wu and returning inferior seed rice to cause famine.

data.entity_name: Gifts Of Xi Shi And Zheng Dan
data.content:
Gifts Of Xi Shi And Zheng Dan
The fourth strategy includes gifting beautiful women to distract King Fuchai and weaken his governance.

Building Lavish Palaces
The fifth strategy involves inducing Wu to build extravagant palaces and towers to drain resources.

Bribery Of Officials
The sixth strategy bribed corrupt ministers in Wu to damage the state administration.

Stockpiling Supplies
The eighth strategy involved accumulation of food and funds to strengthen Yue's capacity for war.

Sowing Discord Among Loyalists
The seventh strategy aimed to cause internal strife in Wu, culminating in the forced suicide of Wu Zixu.

Weapon Manufacturing And Training
The ninth strategy is making weapons and training soldiers to prepare for attack on Wu.

Wu Swordsmen
Wu swordsmen are highly skilled fighters whose swordsmanship and group tactics are superior to Yue's soldiers.

Sun Wuzi
Sun Wuzi is the ancient military strategist who assisted the King of Wu and developed tactics used effectively in battles against Chu and other states.

Gan Jiang And Mo Ye
Gan Jiang and Mo Ye were a couple renowned for their exceptional sword forging skills in Wu.

Ou Yezi
Ou Yezi was a master swordsmith from Yue whose sword forging craftsmanship rivaled that of Gan Jiang and Mo Ye.<SEP>Ou Yezi is a master swordsmith of Yue, famed for his sword-making skills, contemporary with Gan Jiang and Mo Ye.

Battle By The Qiantang River
A significant battle between Yue and Wu near the Qiantang River resulting in heavy defeat for Yue and King Goujian's near destruction.

Zheng Dan
Zheng Dan is a beautiful woman gifted alongside Xi Shi to King Fuchai as part of Yue’s political distraction strategy.

Kuaiji Mountain
Kuaiji Mountain is the location where King Goujian was besieged after Yue's defeat in battle.

data.entity_name: Sword Of Gan Jiang And Mo Ye
data.content:
Sword Of Gan Jiang And Mo Ye
The swords forged by the renowned couple Gan Jiang and Mo Ye, celebrated for their exceptional craftsmanship in the State of Wu.

Eu Yezi Sword
The sword crafted by Ou Yezi, a master swordsmith of Yue, whose forging skills rivaled those of Gan Jiang and Mo Ye.

Yue Nu Jian
Yue Nu Jian is the name of the narrative or story depicted, featuring a sword duel between martial characters.

Blue-Clothed Swordsman
The Blue-Clothed Swordsman is a skilled fighter with a scarred face and experienced in many battles, using a long sword in combat during the duel.

Brocade-Robed Swordsman
The Brocade-Robed Swordsman is agile and quick, known for evading and counterattacking in a sword duel, who faces the Blue-Clothed Swordsman.<SEP>A swordsman who attempts to strike Fan Li but whose sword is cut in half by Fan Li’s quick move.

King
The King sits on a brocade-draped chair at the north side, wearing a purple robe and with an unusual appearance, who rewards skilled swordsmen with gold.

Wu-Yue Swordsmen Duel
The Wu-Yue Swordsmen Duel is a staged sword fighting contest involving fighters on opposite sides competing under royal observation.

Heart-Protecting Bronze Mirror
The Heart-Protecting Bronze Mirror is a hidden chest armor worn by the Blue-Clothed Swordsman that prevents injury despite being stabbed.

Sword
The sword is a weapon used by the duelists, including a long sword more than five feet long with a thick blade.<SEP>A thin and sharp sword with a trembling blade that appears fragile but is exceptionally sharp and durable against heavy weapons.

Burly Man
The Burly Man is a large and robust fighter carrying a long, heavy sword, competing on the brocade-robed swordsmen's side in the duel.

Blood
Blood is the fluid discharged from the Brocade-Robed Swordsman when fatally wounded in the throat during the duel.

Wu Jianfeng
Wu Jianfeng is a skilled swordsmith whose sharp swords are unmatched by other states.

Feng Shige
Feng Shige is a swordsmith who is exhausted from forging a sword for a year and violently attacks Xue Zhuo due to distrust.

Xue Zhuo
Xue Zhuo assists in sword forging by advising the swordsmith but becomes a victim of violence inflicted by Feng Shige.

Xishan
Xishan is a mountain guarded by troops under Wu Zixu to prevent tin mining.

Tin
Tin is a crucial metal resource located in the Yue state, important for sword casting.

Copper
Copper is a metal resource available in both Wu and Yue states, used for sword forging.

Lead
Lead is not mentioned directly, excluded.

Yi Guang
Yi Guang is a peerless beauty embodying the spirit of Yue’s mountains and waters, personally found and sent by Fan Li.

Fu Chai
Ruler opposed by King Goujian, who sent eight swordsmen to deliver the sword as a warning.<SEP>Fu Chai is the ruler of Wu kingdom who holds Xi Shi, causing jealousy and urgency to build better swords in Yue.

Eighteen Guards
The Eighteen Guards are bodyguards escorting Fan Li during his street walk.<SEP>The eighteen guards who accompanied Fan Li as he advanced toward the palace gate in response to Aqing’s threats.

Eight Wu Sword Fighters
Eight Wu sword fighters are soldiers who recently won a battle and parade drinking and singing loudly in the street.

Wu Country
Wu Country is a kingdom engaged in conflict with Yue Kingdom and known for producing sharp swords.

Street
The main street where confrontations and events take place between Wu sword fighters and Fan Li’s guards.

Yue Country
Yue Country is a kingdom at war with Wu, possessing metal resources and attempting to forge superior swords.

Sword Forging
Sword forging is the process of refining metal and casting blades, central to the conflict between Wu and Yue.

Wu Shige
Wu Shige is a swordsmith exhausted from forging for a year, whose actions and fate influence the sword forging efforts.

Wu Sword Fighters
Wu Sword Fighters are soldiers known for their combat skill and recent victory in Yue Palace, later drunkenly causing disruption in the street.

Sword Technique Shadow
The faint and elusive shadow of a sword technique that once taught to others made the swordsmen of Yue invincible in the world.

Yue Warriors
The warriors of Yue who became invincible in combat using the sword techniques derived from the Sword Technique Shadow.

Battle at Wuhu
The battle fought at the shore of Wuhu where 5,000 Yue troops wielding long swords defeated the Wu forces.

Wu Troops
The army of Wu who counterattacked the Yue forces but suffered a decisive defeat.

Craftsmen
The skilled laborers led by Xue Zhu who forged thousands upon thousands of sharp swords.

Yuhang Mountain
The mountain where King Fuchai retreated following defeat by the Yue army.

Wu Capital Gusu
The capital city of Wu entered by the victorious Yue army.

Guangwa Palace
The palace of King Fuchai, residence of Xi Shi, where Fan Li intruded with his guards.

Fan Li Longsword Unit
Fan Li personally led a unit of one thousand long sword fighters to penetrate the Wu King’s Guangwa Palace.

Corridor
The corridor built by King Fuchai, in which footsteps sound like beautiful musical notes when Xi Shi walks on it.

Yiguang
Yiguang is the personal name called out by Fan Li inside Guangwa Palace; Yiguang is another name or reference to Xi Shi.

Sheep Sounds
The sound of sheep bleating that suddenly appeared in the quiet night inside the palace.

Aqing
A Qing is a woman whose threatening voice is heard outside Guangwa Palace declaring intent to kill Xi Shi.

Palace Gate
The entrance to Guangwa Palace that Fan Li reached when calling for Aqing.

Spring Night
The setting of a tranquil and fragrant spring night during which Fan Li and Xi Shi share their intimate moments.

Jian
A thin, sharp sword described as thin as paper, related to the swordsmithing context.

Wen Dafu
Wen Dafu is an official or adviser who speaks about famous swordsmiths.

Gan Jiang
Gan Jiang is a legendary swordsmith of Wu with his wife Mo Ye, famous for forging swords.

Mo Ye
Mo Ye is the wife and fellow swordsmith of Gan Jiang from the state of Wu.

Feng Huzi
Feng Huzi is a disciple of Ou Yezi currently in the state of Chu.

Five Swords
A set of five swords forged by Ou Yezi for the former king, including Zhan Lu, Chun Qun, Sheng Xie, Yu Chang, and Ju Que.

Zhan Lu
One of the five swords forged by Ou Yezi, now in the state of Chu.

Chun Qun
One of the five swords forged by Ou Yezi, held in the palace of King Goujian.

Sheng Xie
One of the five swords forged by Ou Yezi, held by the state of Wu, considered the best sword.

Yu Chang
One of the five swords forged by Ou Yezi, held by the state of Wu, used by Zhuan Zhu to assassinate King Liao.

Ju Que
One of the five swords forged by Ou Yezi; forged with mixed metals so it is sharp but not regarded as a treasure sword.

King Yue Yunchang
Father of King Goujian of Yue who forged the five swords.

King Wu Helu
The King of Wu who requested and received some of the five swords.

Zhuan Zhu
An assassin sent by King Helu using the Yu Chang sword to kill King Liao.

King Chu
King of the state Chu, current possessor of the Zhan Lu sword.

King Liao
The target of Zhuan Zhu’s assassination with the Yu Chang sword.

King Qin
The King of Qin who sought to obtain the Zhan Lu sword but failed.

Feng Huzis Fingers
Feng Huzi’s missing thumbs and index fingers, causing him to lose the ability to forge swords.

Long Yuan
One of three swords forged by Ou Yezi for the King of Chu.

Gong Bu
A sword forged by Ou Yezi for the King of Chu, with a continuous flowing pattern along the blade.

Tai E
One of three swords forged by Ou Yezi for the King of Chu.

Forge New Swords
The method or act of forging new swords based on Ou Yezi’s swordsmithing techniques.

The Girl
A young female warrior approximately sixteen or seventeen years old skilled in swordsmanship and combat, capable of blinding multiple Wu country swordsmen using a bamboo stick.

Yue Country Guards
Sixteen guards from Yue country who come to surround and protect the girl during the confrontation.

Wu Country Swordsmen
Six and later eight skilled swordsmen from Wu country who engage in combat with the girl and suffer injuries to their eyes.

Lost Sheep
The sheep killed by the Wu country swordsmen which motivates the girl's attack and demand for compensation.

Ah Qing
The name of the girl who is a skilled swordswoman and shepherdess seeking justice for her killed sheep.

Injured Eyes
The condition suffered by the Wu swordsmen from being blinded or hurt in one or both eyes during the fight with the girl.

Good Grassland
A large pasture offered by Fan Li to Ah Qing as a place for her sheep to graze.

Sheep Compensation
The negotiation concept involving animals (sheep) used by Fan Li to compensate Ah Qing for her lost sheep and prevent further violence.

Shepherdess
A young shepherdess who owns the sheep killed by the Wu country swordsmen and is skilled in swordsmanship, identified as Ah Qing.

Blue-Robed Swordsman
The leader among the swordsmen, who demonstrates the sword’s sharpness by cutting a piece of light gauze in half.

Light Gauze
A piece of lightweight cloth used to demonstrate the sword’s exceptional sharpness by being split into two pieces.

Wu Warriors
Wu country soldiers known for their swordsmanship and application of Sun Wu’s military strategy.

Sun Wus Military Strategy
The battle tactics authored by Sun Wu that Wu warriors use effectively in group combat.

Palace Superintendent
Official who is commanded to send a message to summon Wen Zhong.

Fan Lis Nickname
Local nickname "Fan the Madman" given to Fan Li for his unconventional and unpredictable behavior.

Fan Lis Reputation
Known for being unrestrained, unpredictable, and possessed of unique insights misunderstood by ordinary people.

Wan County
The hometown of Fan Li in Chu state.

Eight Blue-Robed Swordsmen
A group of eight blue-robed swordsmen sent by Fu Chai to present the sword as a challenge and deterrent to King Goujian.

Wei Shi Captain
The Wei Shi Captain bows and asks Fan Li if he is unharmed after the attack.

Wu Country Swordsman (Stout)

Fan Li's Guards
Fan Li's guards block Wu Sword Fighters to protect Fan Li during their aggressive street behavior.
